subject: Dedicated & Private isolation: executive snapshot + visualization request

From: Anika Rao <anika.rao@blueriverhealth.com>

Cc: security@blueriverhealth.com
Date: Wed, 12 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: executive isolation snapshot + annotated diagram for SOC2/SIG review

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. BlueRiver's audit team is prepping for a SOC 2 readiness review and asked for a short, executive‑level summary of how Redwood handles isolation for Dedicated and Private deployments. Specifically they want:

- A one‑page diagram (PNG/PDF) showing control‑plane vs data‑plane boundaries for Dedicated and Private modes
- A short table mapping those boundaries to SIG/CAIQ controls (network segmentation, egress controls, KMS boundary, audit logs)
- Any evidence pointers (existing artifacts) we can point to in the meantime

Timeframe: they'd like to see the snapshot and table by next Friday (2028‑01‑20). Can your team produce an "executive snapshot" (diagram + annotated bullet summary) and a mapping spreadsheet? If there's a single deliverable you prefer we accept (PDF + XLSX), that's fine.

Thanks,
Anika Rao
Director, Information Security
BlueRiver Health

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com

Jonas / Soojin – I'm on diagrams. Draft approach below:

1) One‑page PDF (letter size) that includes: top row = Dedicated, bottom row = Private. Each row split into three vertical lanes: (1) Control plane, (2) Data plane (inference runtime), (3) Customer network / ingress/egress.
2) Callouts for: KV cache boundary, model artifact storage path, KMS boundary (key wrapping location), audit/log export path (control plane only), and recommended egress ACLs.
3) Color coding for "redacted / not-for-public" fields and a short legend for evidence types (diagram, log export snippet, config hash).

I'll sketch the PDF and attach a zone_mapping_table.csv with lane definitions and example CIDR blocks (redacted) for BlueRiver to review. Marissa will help finalize visuals.

Attachments:
- zone_mapping_table.csv (text/csv) — lane definitions and evidence pointers
- isolation_snapshot_v1.pdf (application/pdf) — blank placeholder draft (will replace with final)

Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Architect, Security
Redwood Inference

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com

Date: Sat, 15 Jan 2028 11:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: executive isolation snapshot + annotated diagram for SOC2/SIG review

Team – I put together the SIG/CAIQ mapping spreadsheet and included three tabs:

- Overview: one‑line summary + mapping to our internal artifact names (control plane docs, network ACL configs, KMS scope)
- Controls: row per SIG/CAIQ control with pointer to evidence (doc IDs or drive links)
- Exceptions & Notes: where we recommend redactions for shared diagrams and where we can provide sanitized config snippets instead

Key callouts to surface in the executive bullets:
- Dedicated: physical GPU pool / dedicated VPC; automated routing to dedicated model variants; audit trail separation (per‑tenant logging)
- Private: customer‑managed VPC peering / private control plane; optional on‑prem air‑gap pattern; KMS remains customer‑managed when requested

I'll attach sig_caiq_mapping.xlsx to the Drive folder. I recommend we: (1) include the one‑page diagram as the front matter in the PDF, (2) add the mapping spreadsheet as an appendix, and (3) provide a short cover note that highlights which artifacts can be delivered immediately vs which require a redaction request.

Attachments:
- sig_caiq_mapping.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Soojin Lee
Security Architect, Red Team
